preamble: Lowering of the nasalized close vowel /ĩ/ to close-mid /ẽ/. In French it is the first step of the Modern French lowering of nasal vowels, /ĩ/ > /ẽ/ > /ɛ̃/ > [æ̃] (Quebec [ẽɪ̯̃]), which produced the open nasal vowel of fin, cinq and raisin; the later step /ẽ/ > /ɛ̃/ is a separate change. It reflects the cross-linguistic tendency of nasalized high vowels to lower, since nasal coupling raises the perceived first formant.

examples.from: Old French fin with /ĩ/ 'fine, thin (masc.)' (< Latin fīnum)
examples.note: Nasal /ĩ/ lowered to /ẽ/ in the Modern French period and later opened further to /ɛ̃/; the feminine fine /fin/ kept an oral vowel because the nasal consonant remained.

examples.from: Old French cinq with /ĩ/ 'five' (< Latin quīnque, *cīnque)
Old French raisin with /ĩ/ 'grape' (< Latin racēmum)
examples.note: Here /ĩ/ came from earlier /iein/ after a palatal.

sources: Wikipedia contributors (2026). Phonological history of French. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonological_history_of_French
